purpose: Safely apply recovered original-marketplace evidence to an existing realized sale without changing the sale sample.
original_locator_rule: A qualifying original marketplace locator is necessary but not sufficient. Evidence must also carry listing_identity that proves the marketplace listing belongs to the exact target product family and exact card identity.
identity_match_rules: product_id must match the market record and routed product metadata
listing_identity.series must exactly match one of the target product's accepted series aliases after normalization
listing_identity.card_number must match the market record card number
listing_identity.parallel must match the market record parallel
listing_identity.print_run must match the market record serial numbering
listing_identity.player must match the market record player
listing_identity.team, when supplied, must match the market record team
task_id must resolve to the current verification queue
sale_index must resolve to the stored realized sale
sale date and sale price must exactly match the stored sample
serial_copy must match when the stored sale has one
when both a direct eBay listing URL and stable eBay item number are supplied, their item numbers must agree
mutations_on_success: promote calculated_market_value status only when evidence state warrants it
store original_marketplace_identity snapshot on the verified sale
fail_closed_rules: Product/series identity is checked before a sale can qualify as original-marketplace verified.
A visually similar card from another Topps release is rejected even when player, serial copy, marketplace, date or price appear plausible.
Plain Topps Premier League and Topps Chrome Premier League are distinct product families and must never cross-verify.
Dry-run is the default CLI behavior.
Any identity, date, price, marketplace, serial or locator mismatch rejects the evidence.
A same-marketplace search/category page is not an original-sale locator.

A later active re-listing of the same serial-numbered card is candidate research evidence only; it must not verify an earlier realized sale unless the historical sale event can be linked to that marketplace identifier.
Rejected evidence must leave the market record unchanged.
Verification must never change realized sale prices.
Contribution verification is derived from all supporting market-record sales, not from a contribution-level boolean.
